title: Document
description: One thing a publisher published (WO-047 / Issue #89, design in Issue #88 comment 2 Section 5). A Document records the act of publication and its rights -- never an interpretation of it: severity, impact and Thailand relevance are properties of Claims and Developments (logistics_event), not of a Document. Reuses observation_common.schema.json's provenance $defs so one Document and one fact_* observation carry the same acquisition-truth vocabulary. See docs/situation_intelligence_architecture.md.

source_id.description: Must resolve in config/sources.yaml (checked as a semantic rule, matching event_evidence's own source_id, so the reserved SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE identifier remains usable for fixtures without a schema-level registry lookup).

evidence_layer.description: Inherited from the source's registry governance.evidence_layer; may be overridden DOWNWARD only (e.g. a normally current_evidence publisher's opinion piece recorded as context). Frozen onto every Claim built from this Document (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 6.2) -- the L3 firewall's enforcement point.

evidence_layer_basis.description: Required (non-null) when this document's evidence_layer is a downward override of its source's registry default.

title.description: The publisher's own headline or factual identifier for this document.

publisher_is_originator.description: False means this document is a syndication or aggregation of another; originator_publisher and originator_document_url are then required (non-null).

access_url.description: What was actually accessed by a human reviewer; may differ from canonical_url.

published_at.description: Null when the source states no publication time -- some notices are undated.

updated_at.description: The publisher's own revision timestamp, when stated.

stored_content.description: Default 'none'. 'extracted_text_internal' and 'full_response_internal' are legal only for a local, gitignored working store -- never in this public repository, where stored_content_location is always null.

stored_content_location.description: Always null in the public repository. No article body, cache or full response ever enters this repository -- matching the existing rule on event_evidence.raw_snapshot_path.

rights.description: Snapshot of the effective rights decision at the time this document was taken in (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 5.4), so a later registry change cannot retroactively legitimise or delegitimise an already-published paraphrase. Fail-closed by construction: this object and its publication_use are both required, so a document with no rights block, or no publication_use, fails schema validation.

geographies.description: GEO-* geography IDs or ISO-3166 alpha-2 country codes. May be empty.

independence_group.description: Copied from the source's registry governance.independence_group at ingest and frozen on the document -- except for a conduit source (governance.channel_role: conduit), where it is instead derived from the underlying publisher identity (IG-PUB-<normalised publisher>; scripts/manual_intake.py) so that every publisher transcribed through the same conduit does not collapse onto one independence group (WO-049 / Issue #92 item 1, the B-1 fix).

independence_basis.description: Required (non-null), by scripts/validate.py convention rather than this schema, whenever independence_group was derived rather than copied verbatim from the source's registry default -- in particular for every conduit-sourced document.

publisher_authority.description: WO-049 (Issue #92) item 1: what the underlying publisher of this document is authoritative for, in a structured, decidable form -- required (non-null) whenever the document's source has governance.channel_role: conduit (checked in scripts/validate.py, which has the registry; this schema has no cross-record visibility). Absent or null is fail-closed: a claim from a document with no publisher_authority can never exceed grade B/CORROBORATED (analysis/claim_evidence_adapter.py::authority_covers). For an originator_channel source, authority is instead read directly from the registry's own authoritative_for/qualification.geography and this field is expected to stay null.

authority_scope.description: A structured scope, not a free-text label, so coverage is decidable by set membership (analysis/claim_evidence_adapter.py::authority_covers) rather than string matching.

reviewer_record.description: Required (non-null) whenever decided_by is not 'registry_source' (the D-12-style review act: a named human states what this publisher is authoritative for).

duplicate_of.description: Set when the same content is re-encountered under a different document_id.

superseded_by.description: Set for a document a correction or retraction has superseded.

allOf.description: Matches the retrieval_status/retrieved_at pairing rule already enforced by schemas/event_evidence.schema.json and schemas/observation_common.schema.json.

Extra safety net (belt and braces): stored_content_location must be present and null, even though its own type declaration already forbids anything else. Every Document carries a rights block (required above), so this rule always applies.
